title: How Ramadan Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain Ramadan, the Islamic holy month observed on the lunar calendar, which falls at a different time each year (in 2012 roughly July 9 to August 18). They cover the lunar calendar and moon sighting debates, the revelation to Mohammed in the ninth month, the Quran being read nightly during the Taraweeh prayer, the five pillars of Islam and how fasting fits in, the intention (niyyah) requirement, the sahur and iftar meals, exemptions for the sick and the challenges for diabetics, Laylat al-Qadr in the last ten days, the takbir at the end of the month, the Eid al-Fitr celebration, and the spiritual goals Ramadan is meant to achieve. The episode ends with a listener mail segment thanking listeners for gifts.

segments.title: Opening and greetings
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with Arabic greetings and introduce Ramadan as the current month for Muslims, noting Islam is the second largest religion.

segments.title: Lunar calendar and why Ramadan moves
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the Islamic lunar calendar is based on moon sightings, so Ramadan falls at a different time each year, and that Ramadan is the ninth month.

segments.title: Origins of Ramadan and the Quran
segments.summary: Muslims believe Mohammed received his revelation from the Angel Gabriel in the ninth month; the words became the Quran, which is read aloud during Ramadan, with the Taraweeh prayer each night.

segments.title: Five pillars and the purpose of Ramadan
segments.summary: The hosts describe Ramadan as a month to reconnect with faith and list the five pillars of Islam, including fasting, prayer, almsgiving, pilgrimage, and the creed.

segments.title: Fasting rules and intention
segments.summary: Fasting runs from dawn to sundown starting around age twelve, and must be done with niyyah (intention) for the sake of God. The hosts note the belief that heaven's gates open and hell's demons are chained during Ramadan.

segments.title: Suhoor, iftar, and exemptions
segments.summary: Muslims eat sahur before dawn and break the fast at iftar with dates and drinks, and the hosts discuss the rich meal, desserts like kanafa and qatayef, and exemptions for the sick, including diabetics.

segments.title: Laylat al-Qadr and Eid al-Fitr
segments.summary: The last ten days include Laylat al-Qadr, traditionally on the 27th, believed to be worth more than a thousand months of worship. The month ends with the takbir and the Eid al-Fitr celebration, with greetings and charity to the poor.

segments.title: Spiritual goals and moon sighting debate
segments.summary: The hosts list goals of Ramadan such as self-control, generosity, and time awareness, and discuss the debate over local sighting versus astronomical calculations or Mecca sighting for the start of the month in North America.

segments.title: Listener mail and closing
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck read listener mail and gifts from fans, including woodcarving, T-shirts, cookies, macadamia nuts, champagne, a pillow, and books, then give contact information and sign off.
